newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity front months mixed, off highs.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity front months mixed, off highs.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures front months were trading mixed Wednesday but off morning highs that came on strength of a rumor of an Arizona nuclear power unit outage, industry sources said.

Early rumors circulated that one of the three 1,221 megawatt (MW) Palo Verde nuclear generating units was out of service due to a pump problem, but plant operator Arizona Public Service said the three units were working normally at full power.
"(The Palo Verde rumor) gave the market some early support," said one Houston-based futures broker.

As of 1235 EDT, August Palo Verde (PV) power futures were down one cent at the day's low of $34.65 following a high of $35.50 per megawatt hour (MWh), while September was up three cents at $28.70 after trades at $28.65-29.05 per MWh.

August California Oregon Border (COB) futures were up seven cents at the day's low of $21.60 after trade as high as $21.75, while September was up 12 cents at the day's high of $21.95 after trade as low as $21.90 per MWh.
NYMEX said as of 1155 EDT an estimated total of 73 COB and 260 PV contracts had traded.

In Western power generation news, the two San Onofre Nuclear Generating Station (SONGS) units in southern California were in a startup mode Wednesday morning, with the 1,070 MW unit 2 expected to synchronize with the regional power grid later this morning.
San Onofre's 1,080 MW unit 3, which has been shut since mid-April for scheduled refueling, is still expected to begin ramping up power Thursday.
In Richland, Washington, output at the 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant climbed to 73 percent earlier today.
Also, the 550 MW unit 3 at the Jim Bridger coal-fired complex in Wyoming was expected to resume operation today.
Power futures were also seen taking some support from talk of some transmission problems into the Palo Verde switchyard, the sources said.
Next-day physical peak power prices climbed Wednesday, with trades reported at $47.00 and 50.00 per MWh, up from a range of $39.00-41.00 per MWh on Tuesday for Wednesday delivery.
As of 1230 EDT, NYMEX August Henry Hub natgas futures were trading up 3.3 cents at $2.195 per million British thermal units.
Meteorologists called for normal temperatures to continue across the Pacific Northwest through next week, and hot but seasonal weather over most of the Southwest.
Although triple-digit heat would continue to bake inland cities like Phoenix and Las Vegas, gentler 70s-80s degrees Fahrenheit readings are expected to hug the more highly populated coastal region.
Separately, southbound capacity of the AC segment of the Pacific Intertie transmission system will be cut by 250 MW to 3,200 MW between 0900 and 1600 PDT on Thursday and Friday for maintenance work.
